The same, for the directories under /boot/efi.
AlmaLinux 10 mounts /boot/efi with wider permissions than its efi-filesystem package records (0755 against 0700).

PHP's opcache keeps its JIT code in shared memory, which /proc's maps show as "/dev/zero (deleted)". Only the shared-memory kind, only PHP-FPM as installed by the system: a memory-only file, a deleted file or a scratch file mapped into PHP-FPM still shows. Code a script maps the same way (PHP's FFI) looks the same and is let through too.

firewalld (RHEL, Rocky, Alma) runs on Python, whose ctypes has libffi make its closures in memory-only files. Only the libffi kind, only firewalld on the system's Python: another Python process with such a file stays a (low) finding, and code from a deleted or scratch file always does.
